SR-STR-223.canonical_math_name: Moving genus-five triple gate and compatible paired-small-point interface
SR-STR-223.exact_equations_or_object: The Stage14 triple correction has a fixed-base genus-5 curve model, but the physical problem is a moving-base bounded-height family. A finite zero census is not nonexistence. The reflected local character-sieve exceptional residues mark failure of an easy local-solubility proof and can serve as error control; they are not a necessary sparse congruence satisfied by every triple. The theorem-scale obstruction is instead simultaneous compatible activation of the paired small points/lifts in the moving fiber-product family, requiring a uniform physical-height moving-family theorem rather than a fixed-fiber point bound. Conditioning on an actual raw physical point converts the reflected-square compatibility gate into a genus-three discriminant-square cover with a degree-two elliptic quotient; the physical triple lift still requires the quotient coordinate itself to be a rational square together with the second factor-square condition, recovering the higher-genus moving fiber-product gate. Finite collision ledgers are diagnostics only and do not prove the required moving-family power saving. Stage14-t3--t7 identifies the fixed-base triple curve as a type-4 Humbert--Edge genus-five curve whose Jacobian splits into five elliptic quotients, reducing geometrically to three elliptic types. A physical triple requires compatible lifts/small points on reflected quotient families arising from the same q, with an additional shared-q Pythagorean relation. These fixed-fiber quotient facts and finite rank/torsion tests do not supply a uniform moving-height sub-square-root theorem. Batch19 t8/t9 adds the reflected 2-descent moving-prime support and the Euclid-parameter joint sparse-residue family target as another exact moving-family compatibility gate.
